qs.q: A newborn screening test for phenylketonuria (PKU) primarily measures elevated levels of which circulating substance?
qs.e: Elevated serum phenylalanine measured via tandem mass spectrometry or the Guthrie test forms the basis of newborn PKU screening. Urine phenylpyruvate is a secondary byproduct seen later in untreated disease.

qs.q: A pediatric patient is diagnosed with phenylketonuria, an autosomal recessive condition. What is the typical underlying molecular defect in this class of Mendelian disorders?
o: Trinucleotide repeat expansions located strictly within non-coding regions
Complete deletion of the entire X chromosome during early embryogenesis
Enzyme deficiencies where a single working copy usually prevents disease
Dominant negative structural protein interference affecting cellular matrix
qs.e: Autosomal recessive disorders typically involve enzyme deficiencies where one normal copy of the gene usually produces enough enzyme to avoid disease manifestations. Heterozygotes therefore remain silent carriers.

qs.q: Why is newborn screening for phenylketonuria performed using biochemical techniques?
qs.e: Screening is designed to detect diseases before symptoms appear, such as newborn screening for phenylketonuria. Monitoring is instead used for tracking disease progression or therapy response.

qs.e: PKU results from lack of phenylalanine hydroxylase, preventing conversion of phenylalanine to tyrosine.
Phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency leads to phenylalanine accumulation causing intellectual disability.

qs.q: Phenylketonuria (PKU) is caused by deficiency of phenylalanine hydroxylase. Untreated it causes
o: Severe intellectual disability, seizures, musty odor, fair skin and hair, eczema
qs.e: Phenylalanine accumulates → phenylketones in urine (musty/mousy odor). Blocks tyrosine synthesis → decreased melanin (fair skin/hair/eyes). Autosomal recessive. Diagnosed on newborn screening (Guthrie test/tandem mass spectrometry). Treatment: phenylalanine-restricted diet + sapropterin in BH4-responsive cases. Start treatment immediately to prevent intellectual disability.

qs.q: Phenylketonuria (PKU) is caused by deficiency of
qs.e: Phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency → phenylalanine accumulates to neurotoxic levels. Autosomal recessive. Phenylalanine → normally converted to tyrosine (requires phenylalanine hydroxylase + BH4 cofactor). Blocked → phenylalanine accumulates → phenylpyruvate/phenylacetate in urine (musty/mousy odor). Decreased melanin → fair skin/hair/eyes. Detected on newborn screening (Guthrie test). Treatment: phenylalanine-rest
